name: Vizuely
subcategory: AI visual generation for marketing creative
tagline: Browser based AI tool for generating marketing visuals from prompts and your own images.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Tools in this shape are mostly a nice front end wrapped around image models somebody else trains and hosts, plus preset templates and a gallery. An agent can rebuild that front end in a weekend: prompt box, preset styles, reference image upload, batch runs, local library of outputs. What it cannot rebuild is the model, so you are swapping a subscription for an API bill and whatever quality the open providers give you that month. If the paid version has its own fine tunes or brand-locked style presets, your clone will look visibly worse and you will spend the saved money on prompt fiddling. Worth building if you generate visuals constantly and hate per-seat pricing, not worth it for occasional one-offs.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you pick a style preset, drop in a prompt and optional reference image, fire off a batch to a hosted image model, and keep every result in a searchable local library.
requirements: An API key for a hosted image model provider
Node 20+ and a machine that can run a local web app
Basic comfort editing prompt preset files
whatYouLose: Any in-house fine tunes or curated style presets that make the paid output look consistent
Model upgrades happening without you doing anything
Brand kits, team sharing, and approval flows if the paid tier has them
Someone else absorbing failed generations, rate limits, and provider outages
A usable mobile experience unless you build one
moatNotes: The real asset in this category is tuning and preset curation, not the UI. If the underlying models are all public, the moat is mostly taste and speed.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because generating a good visual is 10 percent infrastructure and 90 percent knowing which settings produce something you are not embarrassed to publish. A paid tool has already thrown away the 200 bad presets and kept the 12 good ones, and it keeps doing that quietly as models change. Your clone starts with zero of that knowledge, and the learning happens on your time at your API spend. For a team, the per-seat fee is also cheaper than one designer spending an afternoon debugging why the local batch job silently dropped half the requests.
notes: The wrapper is a weekend, the taste is not. Budget for the API bill before you cancel anything.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI visual generation studio. No accounts, no cloud database, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for the local library, file at ./data/studio.db
- Generated images written to ./data/outputs as files, DB stores metadata and paths
- Image generation through one hosted provider, read the key from process.env.IMAGE_API_KEY in .env.local, and put the provider call behind a single module at lib/provider.ts so it can be swapped

Features in scope:
1. A generate page: prompt textarea, negative prompt, aspect ratio select, batch count 1 to 8, and an optional reference image upload stored locally and passed to the provider if it supports image input.
2. Style presets stored in a checked-in presets.json file, each with a name, prompt prefix, prompt suffix, and default settings. Ship five sensible presets: product shot, flat illustration, social ad, blog header, minimal poster. Selecting one prefills the form and stays editable.
3. A job queue: generations run server-side, rows get status queued, running, done, failed, and the UI polls every two seconds. Failures store the provider error text verbatim, no silent drops.
4. A library page: grid of every generated image, filter by preset and free-text search over prompts, click for a detail view showing the exact prompt, settings, provider, cost estimate if the provider returns one, and a Regenerate button that reloads those settings into the form.
5. Favorites and delete. Delete removes both the DB row and the file on disk.
6. Download single image and download selected as a zip.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, teams, billing, brand kits, image editing or inpainting, background removal, scheduled posting, any analytics.

Also required:
- .env.example listing IMAGE_API_KEY and nothing secret committed
- A dry-run mode toggled by MOCK_PROVIDER=1 that returns placeholder images so the UI can be tested without spending money
- A README with setup, where files live, how to add a preset, and a blunt note that every generation costs real money
- Seed the DB on first run, create ./data if missing
